newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium says 2 or 3 more Eurobonds possible in '97. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgium says 2 or 3 more Eurobonds possible in '97. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: Belgium could follow up its $500 million (17.5 billion Belgian francs) (Corrects conversion from 12.5 billion Belgian francs) Euro-Asian bond launched on Tuesday with two or three other foreign currency eurobonds in 1997, a Treasury official told Reuters on Tuesday.
"This is the first one. Maybe in the coming months we will do one more...and two or three this year," the official said.

"In foreign currencies we have to refinance the equivalent of 120 billion Belgian francs in 1997. We will keep something like 50 billion in our (foreign currency) Belgian Treasury Bills (BTBs). As a result we will have something like 70 billion francs equivalent to refinance," the official added.

The official said the proceeds of Tuesday's issue would go entirely to refinancing BTBs maturing at around March 25, the payment date of the Euro-Asian bond so-called because it will be listed in Luxembourg and Singapore.
"Our debt in foreign currencies does not increase with this issue," the official said.
The Euro-Asian bond issue is being lead-managed by Morgan Stanley and UBS.
